title: short-form-poc-kickoff-brief-and-decision-rubric
content:
Purpose
This short-form POC kickoff brief is intended for fast-turn engagements (2–4 weeks) where the goal is to validate integration feasibility, measure latency/cost envelope, and produce a go/no-go recommendation for a minimal production pilot. Use this as the single-page guide to align stakeholders, set measurable acceptance criteria, and capture the decision rubric at the end of the sprint.

Context & scope
Customer: Nebula Retail (example)
Customer ask: Add an on-site product-recommendation assistant powered by retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) for web storefront and mobile app; must meet sub-500ms 95th percentile latency for single-turn suggestions and <=$0.0008 per suggestion token cost target in hosted mode.
Scope for this POC (2 weeks):
- Integrate Redwood Hosted API for a single catalog domain (men's shoes) and web UI demo page.
- Implement a lightweight retrieval layer (Elasticsearch) with top-5 retrieval.
- Produce a performance runbook with latency/cost profiles for hosted vs. dedicated options.
- Deliver an evaluation report with quantitative metrics and qualitative sample outputs.
Out of scope: multi-language support, personalization beyond session-level history, on-prem deployment.

Primary objectives (ranked)
1) Technical feasibility: end-to-end integration of Redwood API + retrieval and demo UI functional.
2) Performance envelope: establish 95th pctl latency, median latency, and per-request cost under representative load (burst=20 rps).
3) Quality sanity check: human-rated NPS-style acceptability on a 1–5 scale for 40 prompts, target average >=4.0.
4) Decision-ready report: recommendation to proceed to 90-day pilot on hosted or recommend Dedicated/Private with rationale.

Definitions & measurement rules
- Latency: measured server-side from API request arrival at Redwood proxy to final token emitted. Report median, 90th, 95th, 99th percentiles. Use 95th as primary SLO.
- Cost per suggestion: all-in per-request cost including token charges and estimated retrieval CPU. Use Redwood internal cost model.
- Quality: 40-sample human evaluation, 3 raters per sample, scale 1 (irrelevant) to 5 (excellent). Report mean and % >=4.
- Stability: error rate (%) during test window (errors / total requests). Target <1%.

Success criteria (pass/fail rubric)
- PASS (green):
  - 95th pctl latency <=500ms under baseline traffic (10 rps), error rate <1%, mean quality >=4.0, cost per suggestion <=$0.0008.
  - Recommendation: proceed to 90-day pilot on hosted with configuration notes.
- WARNING (amber):
  - 95th pctl latency 500–800ms or cost between $0.0008–$0.002, or mean quality 3.5–4.0.
  - Recommendation: iterate configuration (quantization, batching, caching) and run a two-week re-check.
- FAIL (red):
  - 95th pctl latency >800ms, error rate >2%, or mean quality <3.5, or cost >$0.002.
  - Recommendation: pause, consider Dedicated/private or architecture changes (index tuning, model change).

Sprint plan (2-week condensed)
Day 0 (pre-kickoff): architecture diagram, access to catalog sample, Redwood API key, ES test index.
Day 1: kickoff w/ stakeholders (30m) — align objectives, confirm sample data and demo expectations.
Day 2–3: integration sprint — retrieval to Redwood prompt pipeline, end-to-end smoke tests.
Day 4: small-scale load test (1–5 rps), collect latency and logs.
Day 5–7: iterate prompts and system prompt engineering, caching keys, prefix-KV reuse tests.
Day 8: larger load test (10–20 rps), measure cost and pctl latencies.
Day 9: human eval pass — collect 40 samples, 3 raters.
Day 10: run fallback scenarios (model fallback to smaller variant, regional fallback).
Day 11: write performance runbook and decision rubric draft.
Day 12: internal review with SRE and product.
Day 13: stakeholder review and debrief.
Day 14: final decision captured and next-steps checklist.

Roles & owners
- Solutions Eng lead: Asha Patel — overall delivery owner, final report.
- Integration engineer: Marco Ruiz — retrieval + pipeline.
- Performance SME: Jenna Kim — load testing, SLO measurement.
- Customer PM: TBD (customer-side) — acceptance sign-off.
- SRE reviewer: Owen Brooks — stability and runbook review.

Minimum deliverables
- Working demo URL (internal) and deployment notes.
- Performance report CSV with pctl latencies and cost per request.
- Human evaluation spreadsheet and sample outputs.
- Decision memo: go/no-go and recommended next steps.

Risk register & mitigations
- Risk: Token cost spikes with long contexts. Mitigation: enforce prefix length limits, use retrieval snippets, tokenizing budget.
- Risk: Cold KV cache causing tail latency. Mitigation: warm-up runs, prefix caching, or use a smaller context model for cold starts.
- Risk: Retrieval quality (noisy index). Mitigation: refine scoring, hybrid search, bump recall parameters during eval.

Decision rubric (how to choose next deployment)
- If PASS: Recommend hosted pilot with dedicated burst capacity for production-like load. Notes: configure auto-cache, conservative batching (max latency 250ms target), and retention of eval telemetry.
- If AMBER: Recommend targeted optimizations (quantized model, sequence length cap) and re-evaluate. Consider Dedicated if repeated tail latency at 95th persists despite config changes.
- If FAIL: Recommend architecture pivot — either move to Dedicated/Private or change retrieval strategy / model family. Provide cost/benefit comparison in the final memo.

Observation checklist & diagnostic queries
- Check per-request token count distribution.
- Check model variant fallbacks (did fallback execute under load?).
- Check for 5xx error spikes and correlated infra events.
- Sample prompt checklist for human eval: 10 popularity-driven queries, 10 long-context prompts, 10 ambiguous queries, 10 adversarial/noisy inputs.

Final decision capture (template)
- Date: _____
- Outcome: GO / ITERATE / NO-GO
- Reason summary (2–3 bullets): _____
- Recommended next step: (hosted pilot / dedicated contract / deeper integration work)
- Estimated 90-day cost for recommended path: $_____
- Action owner for next step: _____

Open questions for kickoff
1) Does customer require logs to be routed to their KMS or Redwood-managed? (security/compliance affects Private option)
2) Can customer share a realistic query distribution for sampling?
3) Any regulatory retention constraints for telemetry?

Immediate action items (post-kickoff)
- Asha: finalize access checklist and confirm demo data by Day 0.
- Marco: provision ES index and provide sample retrieval API by Day 1.
- Jenna: prepare Gatling/Locust scenario for 20 rps by Day 3.
- Owen: draft 1-page runbook template for on-call diagnostics by Day 8.

Notes to solutions team (informal)
- Keep prompts minimal and deterministic for repeatable perf runs.
- Prefer smaller context windows during load tests to isolate retrieval vs. generation cost.
- If time permits add one Dedicated config run to show delta on pctl tails — very persuasive for procurement.

Appendix: quick-test commands (examples)
- curl sample POST to Redwood generate endpoint with retriever snippet (example skeleton).
- locust/gatling scenario name: retail-rag-sampler-20rps
- evaluation spreadsheet link placeholder.

End of brief.

This doc is intentionally compact — use it to run a focused, measurable POC and produce a crisp go/no-go recommendation within two weeks.
